segments.label: Launch & ascent — Kennedy Space Center LC-39A
segments.note: SpaceX Falcon 9 from Kennedy Space Center LC-39A (28.608°, -80.604°); ~9 min analytic ascent to a 185 km parking orbit (schematic arc, real pad and launch time).

segments.label: Parking orbit coast
segments.note: Circular 185 km parking orbit, inclination 28.9° (plane through the pad at launch and the Moon at arrival — the launch-window geometry). Coast 28 min to the trans-lunar injection burn.

segments.label: Trans-lunar coast (4.5 days)
segments.note: Two-body Lambert arc from the TLI point to the modeled LOI point (Moon's position from the ephemeris at LOI). Departure Δv 3130 m/s, arrival v∞ 0.88 km/s. Mid-course corrections not modeled.

segments.label: Lunar orbit (~111 km, 35.3 rev)
segments.note: Circular orbit after LOI (published 100 km; modeled 111 km so that the orbit reaches the descent-orbit-insertion point exactly at DOI). Plane contains the arrival asymptote and the landing site; inclination 88.1°.

segments.label: Descent orbit (111 × 10 km)
segments.note: Descent-orbit insertion lowers perilune to 10 km opposite the powered-descent point; 3.5 revolutions to PDI (DOI modeled at 2025-03-06T10:39:47Z, published 2025-03-06T10:33:00Z).

segments.label: Powered descent & landing
segments.note: Powered descent integrated for the lander class (Nova-C class (Intuitive Machines): 4.0 kN, Isp 340 s, 1622 kg at PDI): 16.9 min, Δv 2066 m/s. Model, not telemetry. Published duration ≈12 min.

notes: Route reconstructed from published event times and sites with two-body orbital mechanics — the shape between the anchors is a model, not flight telemetry.

Anchors: launch 00:16:30 UTC (KSC LC-39A), orbit reached ≈T+44 min, LOI Mar 3 (492 s burn, ~100 km circular, 39 orbits), DOI 4:33 am CST (10:33 UTC), 12-min PDI, touchdown 17:28:50 UTC inside a crater near Mons Mouton (lander on its side).
TLI placed at 2025-02-27T00:53:31Z (published/nominal 2025-02-27T00:58:00Z): the point on the parking orbit was chosen for a tangential departure toward the Moon.
